newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait parliament to refer speaker dispute to court.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait parliament to refer speaker dispute to court.

text.p: Kuwait's parliament decided on Tuesday night to refer a dispute over the election of its speaker to the constitutional court.
After 15 hours of side talks and official debates, parliament turned to the court to interpret an article in the constitution dealing with the election of speaker.
The dispute was triggered by former finance minister Jassem al-Kharafi who said the re-election of opposition veteran Ahmad al-Saadoun as speaker on October 20 was unconstitutional.

Saadoun failed to win an absolute majority. Thirty of 60 MPs present voted for Saadoun, Kharafi won 29 votes while one vote was void. Kharafi said under the constitution a second vote should have been held.
The Kuwaiti parliament is made up of 50 elected MPs, including four who joined the cabinet, and 11 ministers who by law are ex-officio MPs.
